articles.title: Uefa Nations League: How do smaller countries deal with extended international window?
articles.summary: With the international window extended to four games, how do nations like Northern Ireland deal with the additional demands on players and staff?
articles.body:
In years gone by, the final whistle would have blown in Northern Ireland's Nations League game with Hungary and the players would have been heading back to their clubs.

Instead, Michael O'Neill and his squad are back on the road to Slovakia to face Ukraine in the extended international window.

For 2026, the September and October breaks have been amalgamated into one 16-day window, with four fixtures instead of two.

Northern Ireland have made a strong start to the campaign with four points from two matches, but it isn't without its challenges.

But how does it impact a nation like Northern Ireland, who do not have the squad depth or resources of some of Europe's heavy hitters?

Szoboszlai's Hungary latest to draw blank in Belfast

O'Neill 'positive' as NI maintain unbeaten start

For Northern Ireland in particular, the schedule has been gruelling.

Their Nations League campaign started with a 5,000-mile round trip to Georgia, where Shea Charles' 99th-minute winner snatched a late victory.

For that game, O'Neill, his staff and players had stayed in the BST time zone instead of trying to adapt to the three-hour time difference.

With a short turnaround before Monday's game against Hungary - their first home match in 315 days - the squad flew back home overnight to arrive back in Belfast on Saturday morning.

While Northern Ireland kept Liverpool midfielder Dominik Szoboszlai quiet - as they did with Paris St-Germain star Khvicha Kvaratskhelia in Tbilisi - the players looked tired as the game progressed.

"Tiredness will be a big factor," O'Neill said.

"Logistics are a big factor as well in terms of your travel and how that works."

One other factor for smaller nations is injuries and suspensions.

Northern Ireland were already without key players such as Conor Bradley and Ali McCann before Sunderland defender Daniel Ballard injured his hamstring in Georgia, ruling him out of the rest of the window.

Unlike Germany boss Jurgen Klopp, who has the luxury of effectively selecting two different squads , O'Neill has to work with a smaller playing pool.

Of course, injuries are part of the game and can happen at any moment, but the condensed window only magnifies the issue.

"It's a massive factor in the game and if you look at some players who have been injured in the first game, like Dan, they are now out completely," O'Neill said.

"Other countries have had that as well, but you can miss four games of a six-game tournament."

Another factor to consider is an increase in yellow cards, with tired legs leading to a higher chance of picking up a second booking, which would lead to a suspension.

After two matches, seven Northern Ireland players are one card away from missing a match, and O'Neill admitted he found some of the yellows handed out to his side as "disappointing".

While this is the first iteration of the autumnal quadruple header, O'Neill says he would like to see consistency across the scheduling of matches.

Georgia, for example, have had their first two matches at home so have had limited travel and, by consequence, easier recovery from matches before they head to Hungary and Belfast for their final two games of the window.

"There are things in there that create a bit of an imbalance and I know it's difficult to get the fixtures all right," O'Neill said.

"The only thing I would like to see is we have an extra day's recovery now going into the third game.

"I would like to see the recovery periods between every game be consistent."

The consolation for Northern Ireland is that Ukraine will be making that same journey back from Tbilisi before the third game, but the caveat is they have an additional day to recover and have an hour less to travel with the time difference.

O'Neill added that he understands the logic behind the scheduling, but it has "high demands on players in that time".

"It might be difficult to do that [have consistent gaps between games] but I think that would help a lot of the teams, particularly the smaller nations," he said.

"Sixteen days is a long time and there's the travel as well, obviously.

"We're coping well with it, but I think it will be a tough game for us on Friday night."

While Europe's bigger nations have their own in-house resources, countries like Northern Ireland share staff with clubs, which can bring its own challenges in an extended window.

"We don't carry full-time doctors, full-time physios and full-time sports scientists," O'Neill added.

"Other countries are the same, but all our staff work at clubs and we need agreement from the clubs.

"That's a challenge to be able to staff it properly and keep the level of professionalism.

"The big countries don't have that, they have full-time staff and an army of staff to be able to do these things."

O'Neill also has to consider how much to rotate this squad. It's a fine balance between keeping key players fresh, but also how much exposure to give his young squad.

Of the 26-man squad, 17 of the players are aged 25 or under and only three - Josh Magennis (36), Paddy McNair (31) and Dion Charles (30) - are over the age of 30.

Arsenal's Ceadach O'Neill, Everton's Braiden Graham and Kieran Morrison, who is on loan at Sheffield Wednesday from Liverpool, are the three teenagers in the squad.

"I don't want to put too many young players on the pitch in a game like that where they're untried and untested at that level," O'Neill said.

"We want to bring the younger players in to give them the best chance to be able to do well and to build their confidence and to build their reputation. That's the challenge for us."

articles.title: Muere con 32 años la estrella de la que renegó el City tras matar a dos hermanos en un accidente y acabar en prisión
articles.standfirst: El Manchester City decidió despedir a Courtney Meppen-Walter, que era el capitán de la selección de Inglaterra sub-18, tras ser condenado a 16 meses de cárcel
articles.summary: El Manchester City decidió despedir a Courtney Meppen-Walter, que era el capitán de la selección de Inglaterra sub-18, tras ser condenado a 16 meses de cárcel
articles.body: Courtney Meppen-Walter, gran promesa del fútbol inglés que fue despedido por el Manchester City tras causar la muerte de dos hermanos en un accidente de tráfico, ha muerto con 32 años. El fallecimiento de Courtney Meppen-Walter fue confirmado por el Bury: "Nos entristece profundamente conocer el fallecimiento del exjugador Courtney Meppen-Walter a los 32 años. Todos en el Bury FC acompañamos en el sentimiento a su familia y amigos en estos momentos tan difíciles". No se han dado a conocer detalles sobre las circunstancias de la muerte de un futbolista que llegó a ser capitán de la selección de Inglaterra sub-18. El Manchester City prescindió de Courtney Meppen-Walter en 2013, tras ser condenado a 16 meses de prisión por causar la muerte en 2012 de dos personas acusado de una conducción negligente. Kulwant Singh (32 años) y su hermana Ravel Kaur (37 años) fueron declarados muertos en el lugar del accidente que se produjo en Mánchester, y en el que otras dos personas, de 15 y 16 años, resultaron heridas de gravedad. El alcohol no influyó en el accidente que provocó las muertes de los hermanos Kulwant Singh y Ravel Kaur, quienes habían llegado al Reino Unido desde Afganistán en 2001 para comenzar una nueva vida tras huir de la persecución de los talibanes. Meppen-Walter, que en el momento del accidente tenía 18 años, fue puesto en libertad tras cumplir la mitad de la condena. En 2019, mientras jugaba para el Chorley, Meppen-Walter fue inhabilitado para conducir durante 22 meses tras ser sorprendido conduciendo bajo los efectos del alcohol. Se determinó que Meppen-Walter duplicaba con creces el límite legal permitido cuando la policía interceptó su vehículo en el centro de Mánchester. El futbolista fue detenido y trasladado a una comisaría, donde dio un resultado positivo de 85 microgramos de alcohol por cada 100 mililitros de aire espirado, cuando el límite legal es de 35 microgramos. "Sé lo que probablemente estén pensando ustedes y lo que piensa todo el mundo. Seguramente me llamarán de todo, y me lo merezco. Sencillamente, siento vergüenza", declaró Meppen-Walter ante el tribunal. Courtney Meppen-Walter fichó por el Carlisle United después de salir de prisión y militó durante dos temporadas en el equipo de Cumbria. Posteriormente pasó por las filas del Ashton United, Stockport County, Glossop North End, Chorley, AFC Telford United, Radcliffe, Guiseley, Nantwich Town, Bury y Stalybridge Celtic. "Courtney Meppen-Walter dejó una huella imborrable en todos aquellos que tuvieron la suerte de conocerlo y, aunque lamentablemente vivió momentos oscuros —que nunca eludió—, el Courtney que conocíamos irradiaba positividad e inspiración; expresamos nuestras más sinceras condolencias a su familia y a todos los que lo conocieron en estos momentos de profunda tristeza", declaró Jon Gold, presidente del Nantwich. El Bury prescindió de los servicios de Meppen-Walter en el verano de 2025, tras su cesión al Stalybridge Celtic. La Federación Inglesa también publicó un mensaje de condolencias por su exinternacional en categorías inferiores: "Estamos profundamente entristecidos por la noticia del fallecimiento de Courtney Meppen-Walter —que vistió los colores de nuestras selecciones juveniles— a los 32 años. Nuestros pensamientos están con la familia y los amigos de Courtney en estos momentos difíciles".

articles.title: Raphinha vuelve a Barcelona: tiene un pequeño edema muscular
articles.standfirst: Fue desconvocado para el partido de Brasil en la India
articles.summary: Fue desconvocado para el partido de Brasil en la India
articles.body: Raphinha vuelve a casa. Brasil le desconvocó, esta madrugada hora española, para el partido que disputa en la India, el próximo sábado, a causa de las molestias que sufrió ayer martes en el partido amistoso contra Australia, y que le obligaron a ser sustituido en el descanso. Las pruebas a las que fue sometido confirmaron que padece un edema en la parte posterior del muslo derecho y hará la recuperación en Barcelona. El capitán, además, tiene previsto pasar entre mañana o el viernes, en cuanto aterrice en la Ciudad Condal, nuevos exámenes con los galenos culés para ratificar el diagnóstico inicial. La Federación brasileña de fútbol emitió esta madrugada, sobre las 05.00, un comunicado en el que detalló los resultados de las pruebas médicas a las que sometió Raphinha, que sólo pudo disputar la primera parte del amistoso de ayer martes contra Australia. Intervino los 45 primeros minutos e incluso marcó, de penalti, al filo del descanso. Pero sintió molestias y ya no salió en la reanudación del compromiso amistoso. "Raphinha se sometió este miércoles (30) a pruebas de imagen que revelaron un pequeño edema muscular en la parte posterior del muslo derecho. Por precaución y con el objetivo de lograr su pronta recuperación, el jugador será liberado de la selección brasileña. No se convocará a ningún otro atleta en su lugar para el partido amistoso contra la India", rezaba el documento facilitado por la CBF. El extremo azulgrana regresa, por lo tanto, en las próximas horas a Barcelona para recuperarse, en las instalaciones y con los profesionales culés, de la dolencia en el muslo derecho. El club catalán se puso de inmediato, en cuanto tuvo conocimiento que tuvo que ser sustituido por las molestias, en contacto con el futbolista y con la federación brasileña, para conocer su estado y pedir su regreso a Barcelona. El extremo es un futbolista fundamental para Flick: es su delantero centro titular y su máximo goleador, con 14 tantos. La parte posterior del muslo derecho es especialmente delicada para Raphinha, ya que el curso pasado se llegó a perder 26 encuentros a causa de distintas dolencias, repartidas a lo largo de la temporada, en esta zona, y casi todas las veces se lesionó estando con Brasil. El Barça, que tenía a 17 internacionales repartidos por el mundo en este parón, ya padeció el regreso prematuro, hace unos días, de Eric García con la selección española a causa de un edema en la rodilla.

articles.title: El primer ídolo del fútbol y las primeras trampas del City
articles.standfirst: La posible sanción a los de Manchester rescata la figura de Billy Meredith, el primer ídolo del fútbol de la historia, causante de otra investigación a ese club en 1906
articles.summary: La posible sanción a los de Manchester rescata la figura de Billy Meredith, el primer ídolo del fútbol de la historia, causante de otra investigación a ese club en 1906
articles.body: La semana deportiva viene con el foco puesto en Manchester, la ciudad que tiembla con la sanción que se presume le puede caer al City por la constante vulneración al fair play financiero y la poca transparencia en las investigaciones. Se habla en presente, porque ya ni los más viejos recuerdan que es un club manchado por su pasado, por el episodio que se desató en 1905, después de que Billy Meredith fuese acusado de ofrecer 10 libras al capitán del Aston Villa, Alex Leake, en la última jornada para que se dejasen ganar. El galés fue sancionado un año. Era un tipo que no se dejaba pisotear y tiró de la manta: contó que a él y otros jugadores se les pagaba seis libras, dos por encima del tope salarial de 4 que permitía la Federación Inglesa. Y en esa investigación se destapó de paso que los directivos se llevaban dinero de las taquillas, incluido Tom Maley, que ejercía de entrenador. Fueron desterrados del fútbol una larga temporada. Diecisiete jugadores fueron sancionados y suspendidos con prohibición de jugar en el City. Salieron a subasta en enero de 1907. Meredith, antes, ya había firmado por el United. La figura de éste es interesante. Se puede considerar el primer gran ídolo del fútbol. Antes de triunfar con el balón había trabajado de 12 años en las minas de carbón. Terminó siendo el fundador del primer sindicato de futbolistas. Lo que ocurrió entremedias definió al primer jugador que salió en cromos, al que los aficionados esperaban a la llegada del tren. Fue la estrella que marcó el fútbol de la época victoriana. Meredith siempre será recordado por su palillo en la boca. Lo mordía en los partidos porque decía que le relajaba. Era, dicen, un extremo derecho delgado, de piernas arqueadas, con un regate endiablado y una virtud rarísima en la época: centraba como nadie. Con el City firmó una campaña espectacular en la Segunda División de 1898-99, con casi 30 goles, y llevó al club a su primer gran momento histórico: la FA Cup de 1904, con un gol suyo en la final ante el Bolton. Fue el primer título grande de la historia celeste. Luego llegó el escándalo y su traspaso al United, donde levantó dos títulos de Liga y otra copa. En 1921, con 47 años, volvió al City y estuvo cerca de alcanzar una nueva final. Murió en 1958. Aquel turbio episodio se olvidó. Su figura, jamás.

articles.title: Whitley Bay: The part-timers who won a record three Wembley finals in a row
articles.summary: You probably knew Pep Guardiola's Manchester City won four League Cups on the bounce between 2018 and 2021 – but another side did the silverware hat-trick first.
articles.body:
Question: Which two men's club sides have won three successive competition finals at the new Wembley?

You probably knew Pep Guardiola's Manchester City won three League Cups on the bounce between 2018 and 2020 before adding a fourth in 2021 – but another side did the silverware hat-trick first.

Whitley Bay, who play in the ninth-tier Northern Football League, won three successive FA Vase finals between 2009 and 2011 – an unprecedented achievement in non-league football.

The FA Vase, a national competition for amateur teams, was established in 1974; and in more than half a century The Seahorses are the only ones to win it four times – including those three on the trot.

And they did so under the eye of an unassuming IT manager from Sunderland, who used "quiet moments in the day" to plan historic cup success.

Ian Chandler, who had three spells at Whitley Bay as a player, became manager in 2004 and spent 10 years in charge.

It was no mean feat, as any non-league manager will tell you. Instead of focusing on work meetings, Chandler says he spent more time sorting hotel bookings or discussing scouting reports.

His team were inspired by missing out on Wembley in 2007-08, when Whitley Bay reached the FA Vase semi-finals. They lost 4-0 to Lowestoft Town in the first leg, and despite going 3-0 up inside 20 minutes of the return fixture at Bay's Hillheads Park stadium they were unable to overturn the deficit.

After that elimination, Chandler developed a superstition of never again giving pre-match interviews - as the last time he did so was before the 4-0 defeat.

Whether because of his renewed focus, or because of a desire among players to make amends, it steeled the group to make history.

"It's the hardest thing to keep a team together - as soon as players get noticed, they get picked up at higher level," Chandler tells BBC Sport.

"But after we got to the Vase semis, players wanted to stay and prove what they could do.

Despite being a lifelong Sunderland fan, Chandler admits basing his team on Kevin Keegan's Newcastle - with entertainment even placed above winning.

"There was a standing joke in the team, two or three at the back? One time we chased a game with two at the back," he says.

"The Premier League can be so boring; fans want to be entertained, that's what we promised."

Chandler was already a Whitley Bay hero when he was appointed manager by chairman Paul McIlduff, having scored the winner in the 2002 FA Vase final against Tiptree United at Villa Park.

After a slow start as the then-35-year-old with no prior managerial experience found his bearings, Chandler built a talented team which became the envy of non-league football nationwide.

"We played good football. We had pace on the wing, fantastic midfielders, and strikers who were deadly," says McIlduff, who has been Whitley Bay chairman since 2001.

"When we brought them in, it was about fitting the psychology of the dressing room. No-one thought they were better than anyone else, they played for each other."

A growing influence in the side was the 'Whitley Bay Maradona'.

Paul Robinson came through Newcastle United's academy before a career spent across various non-league clubs in the north-east – including Whitley Bay from 2007 to 2013.

Like several other players and staff, he worked with Chandler both in his day job at software company Sage and at Hillheads Park.

"He was my manager at work and football, I was sick of him," he tells BBC Sport. "But it helped get time off for matches."

And it meant he also had an understanding boss if his mind drifted at work.

"Zoning out happened regularly, picturing scoring and winning, what the opposition would be like - hoping they were rubbish so we could have an easy stroll," he says.

Perhaps Robinson's greatest Whitley Bay moment came in the 2010 FA Vase semi-final second leg, when his last-minute diving header in the driving rain secured a 6-5 aggregate victory over Barwell, sparking a pitch invasion.

"Everyone goes to the finals, you were there, you could enjoy it," says Robinson, who is now academy head at South Shields.

"But the rounds before were the bigger games. At home, we would get 2,000 or 3,000 at every game. You felt like a real player. You associate those memories with 90s FA Cup you never think it will happen in non-league."

Chandler played in a 2-0 win over Preston in round two as they reached the FA Cup third round for the first and only time in the 1989-90 season, and they also progressed to round two the following campaign.

Those seasons of success - made The Bay a feared side for non-league clubs across England, and meant they were ready for the big games in a way most amateur sides are not.

"One quarter-final against Biggleswade [in 2009], they turned up in suits and ties," says Robinson. "We thought, this is their day out, their cup final. We won 5-2.

"By the end, teams were turning up afraid of us. We had it won beforehand."

Off the pitch, the team's success had an influence on the whole of Whitley Bay. A working-class town near Newcastle, which had its heyday as a Victorian-era holiday destination, sporting success brought local pride to the north-east coast.

And like any lower league club, that success could only be supported by dedicated volunteers, who went into overdrive before the Vase finals.

They would go door to door across shops in Tynemouth, North Shields and Whitley Bay to raise support. A van selling tickets was parked outside Woolworths on the high street.

"There was such excitement around the whole of Whitley Bay - every shop had things in the windows, the blue and white stripes," says one of the volunteers, Jenn Robinson.

She got involved because her late husband Mike was a club board member and if she wanted to see him she "had to go around there".

"Everyone wanted to come and watch, we got so many local sponsors," adds Jenn.

"I still do buffets and things for players and long-standing fans. We have a game tonight, and I'm making the sandwiches now."

Newcastle United helped out with selling tickets for the finals, while North Tyneside Council provided security services as thousands flocked to Hillheads Park for big cup games.

But even the best laid plans can go awry.

"We organised a train down to London, the guarantee was that it would go straight to Wembley," says McIlduff. "The first time it worked, second time they were taken to Kings Cross - we had to organise taxis up to Wembley."

By hook or by crook, The Seahorses army made it three times to the national stadium. Some even got royal treatment.

"It was absolutely surreal, and a delight," Jenn says. "The first Wembley final we played at, it had just opened. My husband being on the board, we sat in the royal box, which was fabulous.

"One of the security guys showing me to our seats said, 'Miss Robinson, this is Prince William's seat'. He hadn't even sat in it at that point."

Chandler, whose son Benjamin was a mascot at all three finals, said it was an overwhelming experience at times for the players too.

"The first year was crazy, everything was brand new," he says. "The first year the bus driver scraped the side up of the bus driving into the ground.

"The second year we tried to take everything in, all the lads had their mobiles. Then the third year, it was just a case of can we do it, win three in a row."

And three times, Whitley Bay rose to the occasion.

After beating Glossop North End 2-0 in 2009 in front of 12,200 supporters, Whitley Bay returned a year later to thrash Wroxham 6-1.

The opening goal was scored by prolific striker Paul Chow after only 21 seconds. At the time this was the quickest goal in a Wembley final and was only surpassed 13 years later when Ilkay Gundogan scored for Manchester City inside 13 seconds in the FA Cup final.

The hat-trick was completed in 2011 with a frantic 3-2 win over Coalville Town, who equalised twice before Chow was again the hero with an 86th-minute winner.

In total, nearly 30,000 fans were in the stands across the three finals.

After each final, Whitley Bay celebrated in The Green Man pub just 15 minutes' walk from the famous Wembley arch.

"In the first year we just went back to the bar and it was an anti-climax," Robinson says. "The second and third years the club got their act together and we rented a room; families, friends and fans were invited, they were brilliant nights.

"In 2010, we actually spent 10 days together - the week of the final we spent as a squad preparing, then we went to Marbella for five nights. Best 10 days of my life!"

The 2010 trophy lift was perhaps the most emotional though, as the players were joined by former team-mate Mark Taylor. He had played in the previous year's final, before being diagnosed with motor neurone disease, forcing an early retirement.

"Mark used to come on the away trips after he got diagnosed, he just wanted to be Mark - we had a good laugh everywhere we went," says Chandler. "He's still knocking about, abusing me on Facebook. He was the core of our second and third year."

Success ensured the lives of Chandler and his team were never quite the same again. Reporters turned up to Sage to speak with the manager and his players; even Chandler's mum was interviewed by BBC Radio Newcastle legend Paul Dixon.

Chandler - and his wife - even got up close and personal with managerial icons.

"I was invited to the annual sports awards in Manchester. There were people there like Sven Goran Eriksson and Sir Alex Ferguson [and] numerous others," he says.

"I had my wife with me and Sven came over gave her a peck on the cheek - she wasn't aware of who it was until I told her later that evening."

Robinson admitted that going back to work at an IT company after Wembley glory was a "massive comedown".

"One year I got a standing ovation when I walked into the office, but after that it was just back to normal," he says.

"People wind you up about it - 'are you talking about Wembley again? Give it a rest Robbo!"

Like all good things, Whitley Bay's golden era came to an end. Chandler departed in 2014 after a dip in form; the club have not won a major honour since the 2011 FA Vase and remain in the ninth tier.

But the memories in the football-mad north-east remain.

"Me and my wife went out on a Sunday at a pub in Durham just a few weeks back, and this guy came up out the blue and asked, 'Are you Ian Chandler?'" he laughs.

"Then he started talking about that team; in the north-east, everyone follows football. It was so lovely."

articles.title: Man City guilty charges: Which transfers and trophies happened during Premier League 'sham'?
articles.summary: BBC Sport analyses Manchester City's dominance of English football during the period in which they were breaching financial rules.
articles.body:
Outside Manchester City 's Etihad Stadium is a lustrous silver statue of Sergio Aguero - mouth agape in ecstasy, kit swirling over his head - depicting his goal celebration after securing the club's first Premier League title.

It is the immortalisation of the most famous goal in English league football history, when City snatched the trophy away from Manchester United in the dying seconds of the 2011-12 season.

But what if the goal never happened? What if Aguero had never played for the club? What if City had opted to abide by football's financial rules instead of purposefully breaking them through a "disguised funding scheme"?

The revelation that the club has been found guilty of the charges brought against it by the Premier League three and a half years ago has left football fans around the world questioning the legitimacy of City's achievements between 2009 and 2018, when they were the most successful club in English football and cemented themselves among the global game's elite.

Some fans are referring to it as the asterisk era, and there is a possibility City could be retroactively stripped of the honours they earned during the period, with some clubs seeking legal advice over potential financial compensation.

So how exactly did City's "hugely overstated" income impact their actions in the transfer market, how key were the players who were brought in, and what does it all mean for both the past and the future?

How powerful was Man City's transfer spending during rules breach era?

Manchester City spent about £1.2bn on new players in the transfer windows between summer 2009 and January 2018.

In that time, the club won seven major trophies - three Premier Leagues, one FA Cup, and three EFL Cups - having previously gone without a significant honour since 1970.

The players they purchased during that time included some of the world's best, in all areas of the pitch. Multiple were signed for figures in the tens of millions every summer and made a huge contribution to the club's consistent success.

The graphic below demonstrates how much City spent in each summer and across the whole time period, and contrasts it with the amount of money that the commission which has found the club guilty determined had been falsely pumped into the club by its owners, under the guise of sponsorship income.

City did not only generate revenue from sponsorship funds in that time. And income is also spent on many things other than transfers, including player wages, utilities, insurance, infrastructure, marketing, foundations and more.

But the figures underline the fact that City would simply not have been able to purchase the quantity and quality of players they signed during their era of domination had they not been conducting what the commission described as a "concerted campaign to falsify" their financial accounts.

If City's financial power had been slashed by the extra £830m the commission says they falsely added to their books from sponsorships which were in large part funded by their owners, their transfer spend would surely have been massively reduced.

Add in money from falsely reported image rights and contracts and the total reaches £920m.

Chop the amount in half, say, and maybe they would only have brought in half the amount of players. Or the same amount, but heavily reduced in quality.

Which potentially means no Aguero, no David Silva, no Yaya Toure, no Kevin de Bruyne, or at least a significant reduction in the number or ability of the less glamorous players who were key cogs in the trophy-winning machine.

Would those successes have been achieved had the rule breaking not been going on in tandem? And what would the impact have been on all the other clubs who have played in the Premier League during that time?

Nobody will ever know. The seasons cannot be replayed. And so the outcomes exist in a kind of mixed reality where the world watched them happen, but isn't sure if they're really 'real'.

The era provided the foundation for City's ongoing success, too, meaning more trophies and TV income, and the chaos of the situation has also unleashed doubt about the present and future.

What does it all mean for football fans and the future?

A quick quiz question - what do The Wizard of Oz, Super Mario Bros 2 and the ninth season of Dallas all have in common?

Feel free to grab yourself a hot drink and mull it over for a moment.

If you figured out that the plots of all three never really happened - because in their endings it was revealed that they existed only in the dreams of one of the lead characters - then very well done indeed.

So do the guilty verdicts mean the Premier League seasons between 2009-10 and 2017-18 should now be considered a figment of our collective imaginations too?

City have until Friday to mount an appeal. If that appeal is unsuccessful, then, at some point, the club will be given some sort of punishment.

Whether sanctions will retcon the past in any way is unknown.

And about moving forwards? Right now football fans, both of City and other clubs across the country, do not know whether the football they are watching is 'real' or not.

Are City actually top of the league and in a title challenge, or will they be docked points later in the season?

If they are linked with another team's star player, could that transfer happen or will they be unable to make deals at some point?

Will they be in the Premier League next season or will they be expelled and will there need to be a quite significant rejigging of the pyramid to accommodate them somewhere else?

And then there are questions about what comes later down the line.

Is anybody else breaking rules right now, which fans will only find out about in the future?

Does the potential for years of results to be retroactively kiboshed undermine the Premier League's popularity with fans, players and sponsors?

And can the action fans are watching week in, week out ever fully be trusted again?

The answers to those questions will determine the future of the biggest league in the world's most popular game.

articles.title: The Premier League footballers studying to be sporting directors
articles.summary: Kiernan Dewsbury-Hall, Taiwo Awoniyi and others have been juggling education with a football career - even studying on the team bus during away trips.
articles.body:
The scene resembles an Oxbridge graduation ceremony, but those gathered in caps and gowns are in fact Premier League footballers or former players who have won major honours in Europe and around the world.

The 2026 cohort of graduates from the PFA Business School includes Everton midfielder Kiernan Dewsbury-Hall, Coventry City striker Taiwo Awoniyi and a host of well-known figures.

In the event at Arsenal's Emirates Stadium, Cesar Azpilicueta tells the group how studying on the morning of the 2021 Champions League final helped take his mind off the occasion before he captained Chelsea to a 1-0 win over Manchester City in Porto.

Dewsbury-Hall, 28, travelled by train from Merseyside to London to attend the ceremony and, despite being in the best form of his career, explains why he had completed a postgraduate diploma in global football sport directorship.

The former Leicester City and Chelsea player tells BBC Sport: "I hope I've got a long time left in football. But as a person, I'm always trying to learn and develop away from the pitch. I don't want to stop playing and then just sit around doing nothing.

"This was something that genuinely interested me. Whether I use it in the future, we'll see, but it's always good to do it now rather than wait until you've finished playing.

"If the time ever comes when an opportunity presents itself, luckily I've got something that can help me."

The assembled players are potential leaders in football's future.

Awoniyi, 29, joined Coventry from Nottingham Forest during the summer, and he remains part of Nigeria's squad as they attempt to qualify for the 2027 Africa Cup of Nations.

The striker has also continued his studies throughout his playing career.

"I've got a degree in business management and another diploma, so this is my third qualification," he says.

Awoniyi's father, Solomon, has previously spoken about his strict approach to education. At times it almost prevented his son from pursuing a career in football, but Awoniyi progressed from the Imperial Soccer Academy to Liverpool before making his name in German football with Union Berlin.

"I say to people I am a quiet dreamer," says Awoniyi, who was born in Ilorin, Nigeria. "I always felt education was important. It was a promise I made to my dad that if I played football, I would keep studying.

"That's what I have done and I am proud of it."

Awoniyi points to the "ups and downs" he has experienced as a footballer, referencing the serious injury he suffered in May 2025 when he was placed in a medically induced coma after rupturing an intestine in a collision with a goalpost when playing for Nottingham Forest against Leicester City.

To him, it is important to keep improving and to recognise there is more to life than football, which is where the Professional Footballers' Association course comes in.

Awoniyi says: "It's not like a 9-5 job in football. We go in and sometimes finish quite early and, although it's challenging, I think every footballer has time in the evening for something like this business school.

"Of course, it demands a lot from you and it's all about how willing you are to do it. I say to people there are a lot of things that are bigger than football.

"Yes, football is our passion, but we are normal human beings as well and maybe that's something the world doesn't always see."

The graduates certainly appear no different from anyone else celebrating an academic achievement, exhibiting their pride.

Awoniyi has brought members of his extended family to the ceremony, while Dewsbury-Hall seeks out former Everton midfielder Tim Cahill, now working in Qatari football, to discuss the art of scoring goals.

"Obviously there are stereotypes around footballers," Dewsbury-Hall says.

"But in every industry there are smart people and there are people who aren't so smart. You'd be surprised how many intelligent people there are in football.

"Maybe some players just don't want to do things like this, but they easily could. It's just not their passion.

"I'm not saying this is my passion, but it's something I've done to show that footballers can complete these kinds of courses while they're still playing. Who knows where it will lead?"

The course is designed to run alongside a football career. Seminars are scheduled to minimise clashes with matches and training sessions.

Players can study in their own time, although Dewsbury-Hall says he has had some "weird looks" while studying on an iPad during journeys home from away games.

For Wycombe Wanderers defender Steve Cook, who captained Bournemouth in the Premier League earlier in his career, the course marked a return to formal education for the first time since his school days. Having already obtained coaching badges, he knows he is approaching the end of his playing career.

Some may not actively use their newly gained expertise for many years. All will benefit in some way, though, believes Azpilicueta.

"It's not only about preparing for life after football. It's about becoming a better version of yourself in your football career as well," the former Spain defender, who retired from playing at the end of last season, tells BBC Sport.

Education has been part of his life and is what helped him become a leader on and off the pitch.

Azpilicueta built a career after turning professional with hometown club Osasuna at the age of 17.

He had continued studying until that point and, after abandoning his degree when he became a professional footballer, he later returned to complete an MBA at Harvard University in the United States during his nine-year spell at Chelsea.

The desire to study before playing the biggest match of his club career, Chelsea's Champions League final triumph five years ago, indicates how he balanced his two interests.

"Normally I'd have a nap after lunch if the game was later in the day, but that day it was impossible. You could hear the fans and you knew a big game was coming up. Having my studies also helped me focus and improve myself away from football," he explains.

After ending his playing days with Atletico Madrid and Sevilla, Azpilicueta says he will not be rushing into his next role.

The PFA course includes sessions from prominent figures, such as Brighton chief executive Paul Barber, designed to help students understand how different areas of the football industry operate.

For now, many remain focused on playing football. But among this year's graduates might be future coaches, executives and sporting directors who go on to influence the game in different ways.

articles.title: World Grand Prix Darts: Luke Humphries 'hates' added title pressure from Luke Littler's shock early exit in Leicester
articles.summary: Luke Humphries is now favourite to win the World Grand Prix title after Luke Littler's early exit to Luke Woodhouse; Humphries discussed the added pressure he faces after a first-round win over Dave Chisnall he labelled 'one of the worst performances' he has played
articles.body:
Humphries - the 2023 champion and a runner-up the last two editions of the double-start major - produced a lacklustre performance during his straight-sets victory over Dave Chisnall at the Mattioli Arena.

The world No 2 hit under 27 per cent of his checkout attempts and averaged 80.41, his lowest in the tournament since 2022, although was relieved to avoid joining Littler and Michael van Gerwen in being beaten in the first round.

"That's arguably one of the worst performances I've played on the World Grand Prix stage for myself," Humphries said after the victory. "I didn't feel comfortable throughout the whole game.

"Doubles weren't going in at the start, the scoring was rubbish and I felt like Chizzy [Dave Chisnall] just wasn't at his best there at all."

"It wasn't a good performance, but I'm through and when I play Jermaine [Wattimena] on Thursday I'm hoping you won't see that!"

Humphries is now the favourite to lift the trophy following defending champion Luke Littler's shock defeat to Luke Woodhouse, but admits he feels added pressure with the world No 1 no longer in the field as a title contender.

"I hate it when he loses because it always puts the pressure on myself and then everyone is like 'this is yours to win' and all this type of stuff," Humphries added.

"I hate it when he loses because I want to play him in finals. I want to beat him in finals. I don't want to lose to him in finals, but I like playing in finals because it gets me up for it.

"When he loses, I'm not like jumping for joy. It puts all the pressure on myself and maybe sometimes it doesn't help me.

"I'd rather him still be in the tournament and be the favourite and then I can just backdoor it to the final!"

Humphries' 2023 win was his maiden PDC-ranked TV title and sparked a dominant run to end the season, but 'Cool Hand' has since suffered a string of runner-up finishes in major tournaments following his World Masters and Premier League triumphs last year.

"I feel like I deserve a major - it's been like six or seven I've lost in the final," Humphries explained. "I played really good in the Premier League final and the World Masters final - I played 105 averages and lost, so they are tough to take.

"If you just play anybody else in the world they're probably not going to beat you, but when you're playing a phenom like Luke [Littler], he can beat you. I feel like I deserve one, but sometimes you don't always get what you deserve in life.

"It's up to me to win another four games and perform a lot better than that, because if I perform that again, I'll be very lucky to make it to the quarters and semis."

Humphries explains face 'injury': 'I don't have that great story!'

The former world champion sparked confusion on social media after taking to the stage with a noticeable scab on his head, but felt no ill-effects from it as he progressed to the last 16.

"I really wanted to bring up some amazing story about how I fought five guys off and they come off worse than me, but unfortunately I don't have that great story," Humphries said.

"I did Bullseye filming on Tuesday, woke up Wednesday with a massive rash on the side of my head and it just got worse and worse and then it scabbed over.

"The only thing I can think of is when you do TV shows they put make up on and all these types of things, all these creams, and I got an allergic reaction to it.

"Unfortunately there is no great story to tell, that is what I think it is but I don't know. I haven't seen a doctor but it just looks like I've had an allergic reaction to stuff they've put on my head and face, but I'm fully well."

articles.title: Don Javier, el rey del taco
articles.standfirst: Sobran los motivos, por Alberto R. Barbero
articles.summary: Sobran los motivos, por Alberto R. Barbero
articles.body: Para cuando regrese la competición doméstica, tres semanas después, bastantes aficionados tendrán que hacer un ejercicio de memoria al objeto de de recordar la clasificación de su equipo, si hay motivo para la alegría o para la desazón, lo que por otra parte vendría a insistir en eso de que el fútbol apenas es lo más importante entre las cosas menos importantes. Desafortunadamente para ellos, no obstante, los hinchas del Valencia no formarán parte de ese nutrido grupo. Porque, habiéndose embolsado su equipo apenas cuatro de los 21 puntos que hasta ahora ha ofrecido la Liga como botín, tienen claro, demasiado claro, que deportivamente hablando están en la mierda. Y por eso el suyo ha sido el primer entrenador destituido, debate distinto sería si Carlos Corberán no perdió en realidad hace tiempo esa confianza que de forma oficial se le ha retirado recién, debate distinto volvería a ser, por supuesto, el papel de la propiedad en los tumbos que viene dando de un tiempo a esta parte una entidad histórica. El caso es que, como antes llegaron tantos otros, incluido el propio Corberán, ahora ha llegado el 'Vasco'. De momento para sugerir ese titular maravilloso, 'Esperanza Aguirre', con que nos obsequiaron los compañeros de 'Superdeporte'. Porque eso es lo que trae en la valija el mexicano, escrito no hace tanto el epílogo de un Mundial en el que permitió soñar a su país: esperanza. Nada más. Nada menos... A un tipo positivo y brillante como Javier siempre da gusto escucharlo, que es lo que se ha podido hacer, tiempo habrá para juzgarlo a la que la pelota vuelva a rodar dando la razón a los que piensan, botella medio llena, que un equipo con Guido o Javi Guerra en la sala de máquinas y con esa cantera al rescate de ninguna manera puede estar entre los peores del campeonato, o a los que piensan, botella medio vacía, que se antoja incluso complicado planificar una plantilla tan desequilibrada. El diablo está en los detalles y conviene recordar, atendiendo al último curso, que el mismo Valencia que peleó Europa hasta la última jornada se había salvado del descenso apenas la penúltima. Que son muchas, demasiadas, las escuadras que caminan en el alambre competitivo. Ha vuelto el rey del taco, en fin. Para soltarlos con esa gracia, para formarlo si resulta necesario. Osasuna, Atlético, Zaragoza, Espanyol, Leganés, Mallorca... y Valencia. Bienvenido otra vez, Javier. Bienvenida, esperanza.

articles.standfirst: Histórico error de Musab Al-Shaqsi (Omán) al quitarse la camiseta que provocó un inesperado desenlace en un hotel
articles.summary: Histórico error de Musab Al-Shaqsi (Omán) al quitarse la camiseta que provocó un inesperado desenlace en un hotel
articles.body: Musab Al-Shaqsi marcó en el minuto 84 para poner a Omán 3-1 por delante de Kuwait; esta victoria permitía a Omán igualar a Irak con cuatro puntos en la Copa del Golfo, además de empatar la diferencia de goles a favor y en contra. Antes de la celebración Omán tenía ventaja sobre Irak gracias al criterio de desempate disciplinario de 'Fair Play' (7 tarjetas amarillas frente a las 8 de Irak), pero al quitarse la camiseta en la celebración del gol Musab Al-Shaqsi fue sancionado con amarilla. La sanción a Musab Al-Shaqsi anuló de forma automática la única ventaja que poseía el conjunto omaní sobre el iraquí. Con esa tarjeta Irán y Omán empataban 8-8 a amarillas, por lo que el equipo de Musab Al-Shaqsi perdió su ventaja y condenó a Omán a un sorteo... que se realizó en el Hotel Intercontinental de Yeda. Los integrantes del comité de competición de la Federación de Fútbol del Golfo, encabezados por el directivo Khalid Al-Muqrin, se reunieron en el hotel a los delegados oficiales de Omán e Irak. Tras examinarse los informes firmados por los árbitros de ambos encuentros para ratificar que la paridad en las amonestaciones era absoluta, se procedió al sorteo. Afortunadamente para Musab Al-Shaqsi su selección ganó el sorteo y se clasificó para las semifinales de la Copa del Golfo.

articles.title: Jess Fishlock set to return as Wales coach for Women's World Cup qualifying play-offs
articles.summary: Rhian Wilkinson says icon Jess Fishlock will be back with the national team if they reach a World Cup play-off final in December – but only as a coach.
articles.body:
Rhian Wilkinson says in-form Wales icon Jess Fishlock will be back with the national team if they reach a Women's World Cup play-off final in December – but only as a coach.

Fishlock, Wales' most-capped footballer, called time on her international career last October.

But the 39-year-old continues to shine for Seattle Reign, having claimed two fine goals in last weekend's win over Boston Legacy to become the National Women's Soccer League club's all-time leading scorer.

Wales, meanwhile, are without a string of senior players for the World Cup play-off semi-final against Albania next month, but Wilkinson says she has turned down Fishlock's tongue-in-cheek offer to come out of international retirement.

"Jess could play forever, she's incredible," the Wales head coach said.

"There was never a doubt that Jess Fishlock could still do a job for us. [But] I think it was absolutely the right time for her to step away after that amazing qualification for the Euro [last year]."

Women's World Cup qualifying play-off semi-final

Fishlock, who has said this will be her last year playing club football, will be on duty with Reign when Wales go to Albania on Friday, 9 October and then again in the return leg in Llanelli four days later.

Should Wales overcome a side who are 36 places in the Fifa rankings – and one they beat twice in the group phase of World Cup qualifying – they will play either Norway or Romania in a two-legged play-off final in December.

Wilkinson has revealed that another recently retired former player, Kayleigh Barton, will be part of her staff for the Albania ties and then Fishlock will have a role should Wales reach the final.

Fishlock previously worked as a technical assistant for Wales' opening game of this qualifying campaign, against the Czech Republic in March.

Wilkinson explained that Fishlock had been in touch before she named her semi-final squad on Tuesday, adding: "I didn't appreciate her saying 'call me up coach, I'm ready', which I thought was mean, but [she was] a wonderful player and a great leader for us.

"If we are able to get past Albania, she'll be coming in as a coach for us for the next round."

articles.title: Scotland: Sebastian Pocognoli’s ‘sad’ Hampden debut as he demands Nations League response
articles.summary: Jack Hendry was sent off in the 3-0 defeat to Switzerland, while Scotland have failed to score in their last four games; they travel to North Macedonia in their next Nations League match on Saturday before hosting Slovenia three days later.
articles.body:
Jack Hendry's early red card effectively rendered his home debut against Switzerland a write-off.

They went down 3-0 in their second Nations League match after the Swiss took full advantage of playing the majority of the match with an extra man.

Scotland have failed to score in four successive matches for the first time since 1971, albeit three of their opponents have been in the top 15 of the FIFA rankings.

"I had a warm welcome from the crowd and that made me feel a little bit sad because we wanted to give something back and we couldn't," said the new boss.

"Even with 11 men, if we had the bad result, we would have wanted to give something, some emotion, something to analyse, something to give a direction about where we want to go, and we didn't have the chance to show it and that frustrated me a lot."

Pocognoli was pleased with his team's attitude but felt there was little else to take from a match in which a Swiss side that reached the World Cup quarter-finals in the summer were able to flex their muscles.

"Not a lot to say about the game, you know- 80 per cent of the game with 10 men," the Belgian added.

"Red card, then directly punished from the red card with a free-kick, so probably the worst situation that we can have.

"We should prefer maybe a penalty and to stay with 11 men and to maybe show exactly what we planned for the game.

"We started quite aggressive, front foot, and then after eight minutes, the game plan has to be put to the side and we just see if the team react well or not with 10 men, and they did their best.

"To be honest, they had a great attitude to just stick together, try to have the moment in transition or set-pieces or something, but it never happened because Switzerland is a good side and they didn't give anything away."

With just one point and no goals from their opening two Nations League fixtures after a 0-0 draw in Slovenia at the weekend, Pocognoli admits Scotland's next match in North Macedonia on Saturday has taken on added significance.

"Yeah, it's important to get a result because it can give a boost to the staff, not only for me but for all the people who worked so hard from the first day," said the 39-year-old.

"We had a good second half in Slovenia, and eight minutes tonight that we can analyse on some good aspects, but we need also a good performance in Macedonia and the result is important."

Goalkeeper Angus Gunn insisted there was no blame game in the Scotland dressing room after Tuesday night's defeat.

"He [Jack] tried to apologise to lads in there but the manager was like, that's football, that happens.

"That's why we're a team and that's why we stick together and no-one's got to apologise for anything.

"Unfortunately, we couldn't dig deep and get a result."

"Hopefully, that's lessons learned, playing the majority of the game with 10 men. Hopefully, we can maybe use that in the future and come out on a positive side.

"That's two games down and we've got two more to finish this camp off.

"We've just got to go and react. It's Saturday night and we've got a good squad. Everyone's ready for their opportunity."

articles.summary: Los detalles de uno de los últimos duelos antes de la retirada de Messi
articles.body: La selección argentina vuelve a la acción este miércoles en Córdoba para medirse ante Bolivia en el primero de los amistosos internacionales de la fecha FIFA. El conjunto dirigido por Lionel Scaloni inicia una nueva etapa tras su reciente participación en el Mundial 2026 y afronta este compromiso con rotaciones en el equipo titular, dando paso a futbolistas como Agustín Giay, Facundo Medina, Nicolás Paz y Exequiel Palacios. Además, el choque estará marcado por la ausencia de Lionel Messi, quien no disputará este encuentro y reservará su aparición para el cierre de la ventana internacional en lo que será su despedida oficial de la Albiceleste. Por su parte, la selección de Bolivia afronta la cita con la intención de revertir su dinámica de resultados y seguir afinando su bloque de cara a los próximos retos competitivos. El equipo bajo el mando de Óscar Villegas llega tras disputar un choque de preparación frente a Paraguay en Estados Unidos y buscará sostener un orden defensivo sólido ante la campeona del mundo. Con figuras como el capitán Luis Haquín y el guardameta Guillermo Viscarra en el eje posterior, la Verde medirá sus fuerzas en el estadio Mario Alberto Kempes como un valioso examen internacional. El partido entre Argentina y Bolivia, correspondiente a un encuentro amistoso internacional de selecciones, se disputará en la madrugada del miércoles 30 de septiembre al jueves 1 de octubre a partir de las 02:00 horas (horario peninsular español). El encuentro entre el combinado argentino y la selección boliviana se podrá seguir en directo por televisión e internet en España a través de la plataforma Movistar Plus+ (M+ Liga de Campeones). Sigue toda la actualidad de la selección argentina, el minuto a minuto del partido y la mejor cobertura del Argentina - Bolivia en MARCA.com y escucha la retransmisión en directo en Radio MARCA.

articles.title: Vivian: "Se ha visto la idea del técnico y sólo hay que darle continuidad"
articles.standfirst: Vuelve al equipo tras dos meses y medio de baja después de sufrir la última media campaña
articles.summary: Vuelve al equipo tras dos meses y medio de baja después de sufrir la última media campaña
articles.body: La temporada arranca tarde para Vivian, que a causa de una dolencia en los aductores ha estado dos meses y medio de baja después de haber arrastrado problemas desde enero, aunque nunca dejó de jugar. El central está en condiciones para disponer de minutos este viernes frente a la final de la Euskal Herriko Txapela y a partir de ahí sumar en la rotación de Terzic de cara a los próximos compromisos de Liga y Copa. “Estoy muy bien y ha pasado mucho tiempo para poder decir esto, poder estar perfecto y entrenar con el grupo con la misma ilusión de siempre”, dijo. Vivian competirá ahora por regresar a las alineaciones. “Hay que trabajar y visualizarse en un equipo que está muy bien en mi posición. Quiero estar dispuesto para dar mi mejor versión cuando me hagan jugar”, comentó. El central señaló que “tenemos un entrenador nuevo que viene con ideas parecidas a lo que estábamos trabajando. Un entrenador puede tener una idea, pero debe adaptarse a lo que tiene y el míster así lo ha hecho. He visto entrenar a mis compañeros y me ha dado envidia de cómo lo hacían. Nosotros también estamos en proceso de adaptación, pero ya se ha visto la idea que quiere el técnico y sólo hay que darle continuidad para terminar de sacar los resultados por los que se está trabajando”. El central inició en el verano un plan de recuperación específico. “Sólo al principio tuve dudas de cómo iba a ser el proceso y cuánto iba a durar, pero una vez que se decidió el programa no he tenido ninguna duda. Ha ido todo fenomenal y en una progresión buenísima. Esperándome lo mejor, no me esperaba estar como estoy ahora”. Y reconoció su extrañeza por las situaciones vividas. “Ha sido un verano raro porque me gusta entrenar en pretemporada. Edin me entendió desde el primer momento. Habernos seguido tanto el año pasado le permitía saber la situación en la que estaba. Supo entenderme y darme confianza. Un jugador siempre quiere el apoyo y el cariño del entrenador y yo lo he tenido”, apuntó. El futbolista no se marca plazos para un rendimiento al nivel que se le espera, “aunque ahora me encuentro quizá hasta mejor que otras veces porque he podido trabajar otras facetas diferentes. Ahora mismo soy mi mejor versión de ahora y trabajaré para mejorar cada día”. Y de cara al duelo de este viernes con la Real indicó que “nosotros queremos ganar cada partido y hay que ser competitivos porque el parón de Liga es de tres semanas”.

articles.title: No hay paz para todos en el fútbol
articles.standfirst: La Asamblea de la EFC escenificó la vuelta del Barça y del Madrid al abrigo de la UEFA, pero la guerra con la FIFA sigue su curso y en el caso del City hay compás de espera
articles.summary: La Asamblea de la EFC escenificó la vuelta del Barça y del Madrid al abrigo de la UEFA, pero la guerra con la FIFA sigue su curso y en el caso del City hay compás de espera
articles.body: Copenhague acogió este año la Asamblea anual de la Asociación Europea de clubes (EFC). Hay relaciones que recobran la normalidad, pero otras siguen más fría que los campos de hielo de Escandinavia. En el deshielo está ya el Real Madrid con la EFC y la propia UEFA. Incluso se vio a Miguel Ángel Gil Marín charlando cordialmente con Joan Laporta en un intento de mejorar las relaciones tras el huracán Julián Álvarez aunque sea para esta ocasión. “La educación, las formas y el respeto están por encima de las diferencias que podamos tener entre ambos clubes, eso no ha cambiado”, comentó a MARCA el consejero delegado del club rojiblanco. Anas Laghari, hombre de confianza de Florentino Pérez, acudió también pero aún como representante de A22, la sociedad que iba a explotar la Superliga, a la espera de que el Madrid vuelva de forma definitiva a la EFC, pero ya queda poco para que esto suceda. En el seno de la UEFA, que ya comprobó en sus carnes la buena predisposición del Madrid y su presidente en la final de la Intercontinental sub 20 disputada en el Bernabéu, la visita del banquero marroquí se interpretó como un buen gesto por parte del club blanco. Al Khelaifi lo confirmó en su discurso, con Laporta ya presente como uno más al frente del Barça: “Al Madrid y a Florentino se le ha faltado al respeto. El presidente ha hecho muchísimo por el club y por el fútbol español. Quiero darle las gracias al igual que a Laporta”. Sin embargo, en los pasillos no se hablaba ya arreglado este asunto de los nuevos frentes: la guerra entre la UEFA y la FIFA, con representantes de ambos organismos en la reunión, y la posible sanción al City. En la recta final de la Asamblea saltaba el duro comunicado de la Premier League contra los citizens. Ceferin se despachó a gusto contra Infantino sin citarle y parece que por ahora no hay ánimo de paz, con UEFA buscando ya candidato como alternativa a Infantino para las elecciones de marzo. “Ya basta, el fútbol no se vende. El fútbol no precisa de reyes y emperadores”. Y en lo que respecta al City, Al Khelaifi deja claro que aún la EFC no se pronuncia. “Tú dices que han hecho trampas, ellos que no. Vamos a esperar a que la justicia se pronuncie”. De la FIFA Gianni Infantino no tuvo que escuchar los ataques de Ceferin. Lo hizo su secretario general, Mattias Grafström, que acudió a la cita. La Asamblea no sirvió para buscar soluciones. Hubo saludo entre ambas partes y poco más según ha podido saber MARCA. En ese momento trascendía que la FIFA había pasado al ataque presentando su respuesta ante el Tribunal de Distrito del Distrito Sur de Florida (Estados Unidos) en relación con la solicitud presentada por la UEFA para obtener una orden de obtención de pruebas sobre el proyecto fallido de privatizar el Mundial. En su respuesta, la FIFA subraya varios puntos clave. Se acusa a la UEFA de una "campaña de desinformación en un intento de influir en la campaña presidencial de la FIFA. La conducta de la UEFA fue de mala fe y con fines de acoso", señalan sus abogados en un escrito al que ha tenido acceso MARCA. La presentación de la UEFA, sostiene FIFA, fue una manera evidente de intentar eludir su responsabilidad por difundir falsedades a los medios de comunicación, como que la FIFA vendía torneos, para favorecer sus propios objetivos. "El escrito de 54 páginas de la UEFA contiene numerosas declaraciones falsas o engañosas sobre la FIFA e Infantino". Así las cosas, por ahora nadie da su brazo a torcer. La UEFA encajó en Copenhague la noticia de la última maniobra de la FIFA sin demasiados sobresaltos. Su idea era y es dar con un candidato, preferiblemente no europeo para que tenga más consenso entre las confederaciones, mientras que poco después Al-Khelaifi, por si había alguna duda, cerraba la Asamblea insistiendo en que no tiene intención alguna de aspirar al cargo y plantar cara a Infantino. Copenhague no fue tierra de paz para todos.

articles.title: Vivian se perdió el Mundial por su compromiso con el Athletic
articles.standfirst: El club le pidió que jugara meses mermado y dejase la recuperación para el verano
articles.summary: El club le pidió que jugara meses mermado y dejase la recuperación para el verano
articles.body: La última Eurocopa y la preparación del Mundial tuvo a Vivian entre los elegidos de De la Fuente. Pero la lesión en la inserción de los aductores, donde hubo una rotura, truncó la posibilidad de viajar a la cita de Estados Unidos, México y Canadá. “Un jugador debe tener ambición y siempre la he tenido. Claro que dolió. Trabajé mucho para estar ahí, pero en ese momento no estaba en mi mejor versión y a la selección con Luis siempre ha quedado claro que van los que están en el mejor momento. Fue duro y difícil, pero también sirve para aprender y recapacitar en muchas situaciones. Tuve envidia sana de querer estar ahí, es normal. Durante el Mundial tuve contacto con mis compañeros y ahora tengo la ilusión de poder llegar al siguiente”, explicó el central. El gasteiztarra explicó que se lesionó en enero, pero que las necesidades del equipo hicieron que tuviera que seguir jugando en vez de trabajar en una recuperación que sí le podría haber acercado al Mundial con un final de campaña a buen rendimiento. “Sabía que podía acarrear. Muchas veces uno sabe que debe sacrificarse de esa manera y saber que el club está por encima de todo. Desde enero tuve una lesión en la inserción del aductor y he ido arrastrando problemas. En ese momento el equipo tenía la situación que tenía y se decidió no parar. Había que ponerlo todo para estar ahí. Durante la semana sufría mucho en los entrenamientos para poder llegar al partido. Me debo al club y me sacrifiqué por ello. Igual no pude estar al 100%, pero hay momentos en los que uno tiene que conseguir que su 80 sea su 100”, destacó. La convocatoria final para el Mundial no tuvo explicación por parte del seleccionador, que es algo que tampoco pedía Vivan. “No hablamos. Luis también ha dejado claro muchas veces de que no dará explicaciones de por qué uno está y por qué otro no está. No me hacía falta porque cada futbolista debe de ser consciente de lo que hace”, señaló. El proceder del Athletic con respecto a la recuperación de Nico fue distinto porque también las lesiones, aunque similares, tenían características diferentes. Nico paró por completo unas semanas y llegó en condiciones de jugar el Mundial, participando en la final con asistencia a Ferran en el gol del triunfo. El camino del menor de los Williams no pudo darse con Vivian.

articles.title: Ángel Haro, satisfecho con el arranque de temporada, "pero con los pies en el suelo"
articles.standfirst: El presidente del Betis cree que aún queda "mucha Liga" y hace falta mantener la "regularidad"
articles.summary: El presidente del Betis cree que aún queda "mucha Liga" y hace falta mantener la "regularidad"
articles.body: El Betis vive uno de sus mejores momentos tanto a nivel deportivo como social e institucional. Más de 20 años después ha regresado a la Champions League, la máxima competición oficial de clubes de la UEFA, y en la competición doméstica es ya de manera recurrente uno de los equipos que aspiran cada temporada a pelear por los puestos europeos. Pero su presidente, Ángel Haro, aunque satisfecho, se muestra prudente. En declaraciones a PTV Sevilla durante la presentación de libro '95 temporadas del Real Betis Balompié en la Liga', de Carlos Bellver. el máximo mandatario del club verdiblanco valora de manera muy positiva el arranque de curso de su equipo, con 16 puntos de 21 posibles en LaLiga y un brillante triunfo a domicilio con remontada incluida en Francia frente al Lille en el estreno de la Liga de Campeones: "Estamos en muy buen momento. Evidentemente es mucho mejor empezar la Liga como lo hemos hecho y también con ese triunfo en Champions". Eso sí, el empresario advierte que lo hecho hasta ahora no servirá de nada si el equipo no mantiene su mismo nivel, exigencia y compromiso de ahora en adelante. "Queda mucha Liga, va a ser muy exigente, hay que seguir trabajando con humildad, conseguir una regularidad porque para lograr cosas y estar arriba hay que ser muy, muy regular. Satisfecho, pero con los pies en el suelo", ha señalado Haro en su primera aparición pública desde la rueda de prensa de presentación de los últimos fichajes de su equipo en el mercado. El Betis ocupa puestos de Champions en la clasificación y ha dado un primer e importante paso para lograr por primera vez en su historia acceder a las rondas eliminatorias del máximo torneo continental. A la vuelta del parón, con cuatro partidos seguidos en casa, dos de Liga y dos en la Liga de Campeones, espera seguir avanzando en el camino hacia sus dos grandes objetivos de la temporada. Con satisfacción por lo hecho, pero con ambición y exigencia por lo que queda por hacer.

articles.title: Northern Ireland: Jess Kelmore one of five new call-ups for World Cup play-off
articles.summary: Sparta Prague forward Kess Elmore is a surprise first call-up for Northern Ireland's 2027 Women's World Cup play-off with Portugal.
articles.body:
Sparta Prague forward Kess Elmore is a surprise first call-up for Northern Ireland's 2027 Women's World Cup play-off with Portugal.

Elmore, 27, is a former England youth international and is one of five new call-ups in Michael McArdle's squad.

Galway United full back Lucy-Jayne Grant is included for the first time, as are the Irish Premiership trio Naomi McLaughlin, Jane McMaster and Charlotte Havern.

Havern has had a strong campaign for champions Cliftonville, while McMaster has stood out for Linfield and McLaughlin has impressed for Glentoran after a mid-season switch back to the league from Aberdeen.

There are several absentees through injury, including Kelsie Burrows, Laura Rafferty, Nadene Caldwell, Megan Bell, Joely Andrews, Danielle Maxwell and Caragh Hamilton.

Captain Simone Magill, who gave birth to her daughter Skye in the summer, has returned to training but the play-off comes too soon for her to be involved in the matches.

Northern Ireland host Portugal at Inver Park on Friday, 9 October before the return leg in Portimao four days later.

The sides last met in Euro 2025 qualifying when Portugal ran out 4-0 winners in Liera before a narrow 2-1 victory at Mourneview Park.

If McArdle's side can upset Portugal, who are ranked 28 places higher than NI, then they would face Iceland or Croatia in the next play-off round.

While the majority of teams who win the second play-off round will progress to the finals in Brazil, Northern Ireland's ranking means they would likely face an additional inter-continental play-off round in February, as the lowest European side, if they are to make a first World Cup.

"I use the word excitement because we've got a squad that's got a good mix," McArdle said.

"It's highly competitive now to break into the squad, but also highly competitive to stay in the squad.

"That brings an energy and, going toe-to-toe with Portugal, that's exactly what you need when you want to try and qualify."

It's fair to say that the inclusions of Elmore and Grant came as something of a surprise for two big matches, but it shows the importance of eligibility for McArdle and Northern Ireland.

McArdle has been dealing with a lengthy injury list, including some experienced names, but has working over the summer to expand the playing pool available to him.

Elmore, whose father is from Lisburn, is a versatile forward and came through the academy at Liverpool before she moved to the USA to play College football.

Spells with St Etienne and Brooklyn FC followed, before she joined Austrian side St Polten and made the switch to Sparta Prague in the summer.

Left back Grant, who plays for Galway United in the League of Ireland, qualifies for Northern Ireland through her County Down-born father and strengthens defensive options.

With time after the group stages of qualifying, Scotland-based McArdle has spent a lot of time in Northern Ireland watching the Women's Premiership and the trio of McLaughlin, McMaster and Havern have been rewarded for their strong form.

McArdle acknowledges it is a long road ahead if Northern Ireland are to reach a first World Cup, but these matches are not only about next summer but the years to come.

Defenders: Rebecca Holloway (Birmingham City), Rebecca McKenna (Birmingham City), Ellie Mason (Charlton), Natalie Johnson (Norwich City), Fi Morgan (Celtic), Abi Sweetlove (Linfield), Emily Cassap (Sunderland), Lucy-Jayne Grant (Galway United ), Jane McMaster (Linfield)

Midfielders: Aimee Kerr (Glentoran), Mia Moore (Glentoran), Brenna McPartlan (Burnley), Keri Halliday (Hearts), Connie Scofield (Sheffield United), Naomi McLaughlin (Glentoran), Charlotte Havern (Cliftonville).

Forwards: Lauren Wade (Hearts), Casey Howe (Celtic), Leyla McFarland (Rapperswil-Jona, Switzerland), Cora Chambers (Linfield), Kess Elmore (Sparta Prague).

articles.title: Ceuta agradece al Betis su gesto por el amistoso de este jueves y llama a llenar La Cartuja
articles.standfirst: El Gobierno de la Ciudad Autónoma muestra su "reconocimiento" al club verdiblanco
articles.summary: El Gobierno de la Ciudad Autónoma muestra su "reconocimiento" al club verdiblanco
articles.body: El amistoso que disputarán este jueves el Real Betis y la AD Ceuta FC en el Estadio de La Cartuja tendrá un marcado carácter solidario y servirá también para estrechar los vínculos entre Sevilla y la Ciudad Autónoma. Una iniciativa impulsada por el club verdiblanco y su Fundación que ha recibido el agradecimiento público del Gobierno ceutí en vísperas del encuentro. Según recoge la agencia EFE de un comunicado del Gobierno de Ceuta, la Ciudad ha expresado su "reconocimiento" al Real Betis Balompié y a su Fundación por "hacer posible" este partido dedicado a Ceuta. El Ejecutivo que preside Juan Jesús Vivas agradece además "de antemano el apoyo de cada aficionado" que acuda mañana a La Cartuja y extiende su invitación a los vecinos de Sevilla y de toda su provincia para que se sumen a la cita. "Ese día, con independencia de los colores de cada uno, las gradas pueden mostrar su cercanía a los ceutíes y ayudar a dar visibilidad a una situación que concierne a todos los españoles", señala el Gobierno de Ceuta en el comunicado difundido por EFE. El Ejecutivo ceutí incide además en el valor del deporte como punto de encuentro en torno a la Ciudad Autónoma: "El deporte vuelve a ofrecer una oportunidad para unirnos en torno a Ceuta, escuchar a sus ciudadanos y expresar el compromiso con la integridad de España". El Gobierno de Ceuta también ha trabajado para facilitar la presencia de seguidores caballas en La Cartuja. La Consejería de Turismo ha realizado gestiones con Baleària para modificar el horario del último barco del jueves entre Algeciras y Ceuta. Su salida, inicialmente prevista para las 23.00 horas, se retrasará hasta las 00.30 horas de la madrugada del viernes. La medida permitirá a los aficionados desplazados a Sevilla disponer de más margen para regresar después de un partido que comenzará a las 20.00 horas. El Gobierno ceutí ha agradecido a la naviera su disposición para atender la petición y favorecer así la presencia del mayor número posible de seguidores. El amistoso entre el Real Betis y la AD Ceuta FC tendrá además una vertiente solidaria. Los beneficios obtenidos con la venta de entradas se destinarán a Cáritas de Ceuta, destinataria de la recaudación de una cita con la que el club verdiblanco ha querido mostrar su cercanía a la Ciudad Autónoma.

articles.title: Los entrenamientos del Barça, claves en el segundo gol de Lamine
articles.standfirst: El de Rocafonda confiesa que conocía como podía reaccionar Livakovic
articles.summary: El de Rocafonda confiesa que conocía como podía reaccionar Livakovic
articles.body: Livakovic era uno de los nombres propios del encuentro de anoche entre España y Croacia. El guardameta del Barcelona regresaba a un escenario muy especial para él, el Ramón Sánchez-Pizjuán, donde había debutado como azulgrana en el último partido de LaLiga antes del parón. Esta vez, sin embargo, lo hacía defendiendo la camiseta de Croacia y con Lamine Yamal como rival, en lugar de compañero. Y ese conocimiento mutuo entre ambos terminó jugándole una mala pasada al portero. El internacional croata llegó al Barcelona el pasado verano procedente del Fenerbahçe y el 28 de agosto ya se puso a las órdenes de Hansi Flick. Desde entonces, Livakovic y Lamine han compartido vestuario y entrenamientos y han protagonizado numerosos duelos en la ciudad deportiva azulgrana. Una circunstancia que el extremo español aprovechó a la perfección en el tercer tanto de la Roja. Era, precisamente, el segundo gol de la noche de Lamine Yamal. El atacante de Rocafonda no escondió que su elección de lanzamiento estuvo condicionada por conocer al guardameta croata de los entrenamientos. El extremo decidió buscar el palo corto, consciente de cómo suele reaccionar Livakovic en este tipo de situaciones y de los movimientos que realiza bajo palos. "Ya lo conozco de los entrenos, ya lo conozco. He pensado en cuando le chuto en los entrenos lo que hace él y, gracias a Dios, me ha entrado", explicó el internacional azulgrana después del encuentro. Para el guardameta croata el reencuentro con su compañero terminó teniendo un desenlace amargo. Livakovic conocía perfectamente las virtudes de Lamine, pero el extremo también conocía sus respuestas bajo palos. Y, en esta ocasión, fue el atacante quien salió vencedor de ese particular duelo entre compañeros de vestuario.

articles.title: Laporta: "Queríamos a Lautaro a toda costa para el Barça"
articles.standfirst: El presidente azulgrana reconoció que habló con el Inter para ver la posibilidad de que el argentino se convirtiera en el delantero de los culés
articles.summary: El presidente azulgrana reconoció que habló con el Inter para ver la posibilidad de que el argentino se convirtiera en el delantero de los culés
articles.body: El mercado de fichajes fue muy bueno para el Barça, pero para muchos, faltó la guinda. Uno de los grandes objetivos era fichar un delantero centro, con Julián Alvarez a la cabeza, pero su llegada se hizo imposible y el club activó el plan B: Lautaro Martínez. Ahora Laporta ha querido desvelar cómo se gestó esa posibilidad, que finalmente no se materializó. "Lautaro es un jugador increíble. Lo queríamos a toda costa para el Barça", reconoce el presidente culé en una entrevista para el Corriere dello Sport. "Les contaré cómo pasó. Un día llamé a Beppe Marotta (presidente del club italiano). Él y yo, sin intermediarios. Le dije que estaría encantado de tener a Lautaro en mi equipo y que admiraba mucho al chico...", contaba Laporta. Pero no se pudo dar. "Ni siquiera me dejó terminar de hablar. Me dijo claramente que el jugador no estaba en venta y que él no sería quien decidiría si se marchaba o no. Así que puse fin a todas las conversaciones. No había manera de seguir adelante. Marotta y yo tenemos una relación de confianza mutua. No fuimos más allá por respeto a él y al Inter", explicaba el mandatario azulgrana. Laporta también fue consultado por la posibilidad de que Cesc Fábregas pueda entrenar al Barça porque el técnico tiene una cláusula que le facilitaría salir del Como para entrenar al club de su vida. Pero el presidente sólo tiene ojos para Flick: "Cesc es de los nuestros y estamos muy contentos con el éxito que está teniendo en el Como, Se lo merece por completo". Ambos se verán próximamente en Champions. "Estamos deseando darle la bienvenida de nuevo al Camp Nou. Fábregas conoce nuestra mentalidad y la visitón del Barça mejor que nadie. Creció aquí y este siempre será su hogar. Nos gusta su forma de entender el fútbol. Ahora, sin embargo, tenemos un gran entrenador como Flick. Y ya habéis visto de lo que es capaz", dijo el directivo.
